tldr: Headlines across all 14 buckets advertise a routine White House succession — Trump picking Katie Zacharia to replace Karoline Leavitt — with near-zero editorial colour. The only divergent headline angles are personal-loyalty characterisations ('devoted fan', 'honor of a lifetime') from SE Asian and US outlets, and i News UK's MAGA-women-pipeline framing, both absent from the factual appointment headlines that dominate the remaining 11 buckets.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet whose headline treats the appointment as a pattern rather than a personnel event — 'The rise and rise of Trump's favourite Maga women' zooms out to a cultural pipeline narrative absent from all other 26 titles.

Only outlet whose headline foregrounds a viral social-media comparison ('Natalie Harp look alike? Images shared online') rather than the appointment itself — a clickbait-first framing invisible in all other buckets.
One of only two outlets (with Straits Times) to headline 'devoted fan' in scare quotes, characterising Zacharia as a personal loyalist rather than a professional appointee.
Only outlet to lead the headline with Zacharia's own emotional reaction ('Honor of a Lifetime') rather than Trump's appointment action — reversing the standard subject-verb framing.
'Trumps neues Sprachrohr' (Trump's new mouthpiece) is the only headline to use an editorially loaded term for the press secretary role, signalling subservience rather than professional capacity.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents an almost unanimous factual appointment story; loyalty characterisation and MAGA-identity framing appear in only three buckets (usa, uk, vietnam_thai_my), and are invisible in the other eleven.
